subject: Compute runway & peaking model for Stellaris commitment
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria@stellaris.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing ask: Stellaris commit and latency SLO mapping

Rachel / Ben / Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had a productive internal alignment meeting and want to move from pilot to a committed Dedicated pool for production traffic. Before we sign up we need a short, concrete plan that ties the proposed monthly commit to the expected SLOs so our infra and procurement teams can sign off.

What we attached: two days of production sampling (small subset) showing peak minutes and an exported request histogram. High-level asks below:
- Map our peak token/sec estimate to required GPU count (preferred SKUs: H100 or equivalent).
- Provide P95 latency projection for our main generation flow (average generation ~35 tokens, tail spikes up to 120 tokens). Our SLO target is 300ms p95 end-to-end for the API (we expect ~50–80ms network overhead).
- Recommend a safety/headroom buffer (percent) for initial commit and a suggested canary plan for the first 30 days.

Timeline: procurement needs an initial sizing by end of the quarter (May 5). Can you confirm next steps?

Appreciate it — Maria

--
Maria Lopez
CTO, Stellaris AI
maria@stellaris.ai
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria@stellaris.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: Stellaris commit and latency SLO mapping

Hi Maria —

Thanks for the samples, that helps a lot. I took an initial pass and attached a draft compute model (redwood_compute_model_v1.xlsx) with assumptions called out on the first tab. High-level answers below; Ben and Jonas — can you validate the numbers and add engineering notes on batching/quantization tradeoffs?

Initial assumptions I used:
- Primary model: open-7B variant (we'll also propose a 13B variant for fallback); baseline quantization profile: Q4_0 for best cost/latency tradeoff.
- Avg tokens / request: 35 (you mentioned 35)
- Peak concurrent request rate observed in samples: ~210 rps (1-minute peak) -> peak tokens/sec = 210 * 35 = 7,350 t/s
- Target user-visible p95: 300ms (end-to-end). We budget ~75ms for network + ingress, leaving ~225ms server-side p95.

From the draft sheet I estimated two sizing points:
1) Sustained baseline: 2.5k t/s -> 1x slab of 3 H100-equivalents (shared multitenant optimized kernel path).
2) Peak+headroom: 7.35k t/s -> ~6 H100-equivalents for steady handling with a 25% headroom buffer.

Open items for engineering:
- Quantized throughput per GPU for the specific model & prompt length (Ben)
- How much concurrent KV cache reuse we can count on for your traffic shape (Jonas)

Next steps: Ben/Jonas — can you send a short validated breakdown (tokens/sec per SKU, expected p95 per configuration) by Tue so I can include in the procurement packet? Maria — if timing is tight we can ship a conservative commit + canary to shorten procurement cycles.

Thanks,
Rachel

--

On Sun, Apr 25, 2027 at 10:30 AM Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Maria —
> 
> Thanks for the samples, that helps a lot. I took an initial pass and attached a draft compute model...

I've validated the numbers in the workbook and ran microbenchmarks against the open-7B (Q4_0) profile with prompt lengths drawn from Maria's CSV. Notes and a concise table below.

Bench summary (approx, measured on H100 logical partitions with our optimized kernels):
- Single H100 (Q4_0, avg 35 tokens/request): sustained ~1,400 t/s at p95 ~180ms
- Single H100 (Q4_0, when batching aggressively for throughput): burst up to ~2,200 t/s (p95 moves to ~260–320ms depending on batch window)
- For mixed length traffic (spikes to 120 tokens): effective throughput per H100 drops ~25% during those spike windows.

Sizing math I propose (rounded):
- Observed 1-min peak: 7,350 t/s -> we should target effective capacity 9,200 t/s to respect 25% headroom and variance.
- H100 effective steady capacity for our fleet mix (practical): ~1,500 t/s (balanced latency/throughput).
-> Required H100s = ceil(9200 / 1500) = 7 H100s.

Latency fit: with 7 H100s and our request routing + prefix caching enabled, expected server-side p95 ~210ms (network + ingress budget still applies -> end-to-end p95 ~285ms). That meets the 300ms target with a modest margin.

Operational notes and mitigations:
- Canary plan: start with a 3-H100 dedicated slab (approx 45% of required) for a 2-week canary using sampled production traffic routed through canary; if error rates/latency stable, phase to full 7-H100 commit over 10 business days.
- Fallback: if we see badly skewed spikes in token length, automatic fallback to a smaller but faster model variant (quantized 7B low-latency profile) keeps p95 under 400ms while we autoscale.

I'll attach a compact table in the workbook with the latency vs GPU count curves.

Ben

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria@stellaris.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: Stellaris commit and latency SLO mapping

Thanks team — quick operational checklist and a final recommendation for procurement.

Confirmations based on Ben's bench and the traffic samples:
- Effective tokens/sec per H100 that we can rely on in a multi-tenant dedicated pool with caching = 1.3–1.5k t/s. I used 1.375k t/s for conservative math.
- Peak projection -> 7.35k observed -> target capacity w/headroom = 9.2k t/s -> 7 H100s (as Ben recommended).
- Suggested initial commit: 7 H100s reserved (monthly) with a 30% burst pool (on-demand) for unexpected peaks. That maps to: 7 reserved + 2 burst H100-equivalents.

Operational rollout (recommended):
1) Procurement signs for 7 reserved H100s with an agreed 30% burst window for 90 days.
2) Day 0–7: Canary on 3 reserved H100s (traffic split 10%). Collect p95/err metrics and KV cache hit rates.
3) Day 8–14: Expand to 5 reserved H100s (traffic 40%).
4) Day 15–21: Move to 7 reserved H100s and enable burst policy.

Deliverables I'll provide by EOD Wed:
- One-page SLA fit summary (p95 projections, expected error budget consumption).
- A short runbook for the canary (routing rules, rollback triggers, telemetry thresholds).

Maria — if that schedule works I'll push the final quote and the procurement artifact (terms + DocuSign link) to the HubSpot deal.

Jonas
